correctness.rationale: Exact double Fourier coefficients match the weighted half-time heat convolution by the identity ((n+m)/2)^2=(n²+m²)/2-j² for n-m=2j. The heat convolution has dense trigonometric range since multipliers never vanish, proving necessity of w>=0. A nonzero finite trigonometric polynomial w>=0 is positive a.e.; convolution of any nonzero finite measure is nonzero, proving strictly positive measure energy and C-universality. Quadratic minimization and exact -1/10 finite-Fourier witness confirm sharp two-harmonic/one-harmonic claims. Standalone rational checker passed 9206 tests; they supplement proof.

value.rationale: A natural periodic thermal covariance family with arbitrary finite sum-coordinate harmonic modulation receives a complete and computable exact positivity classification. The sharp one-harmonic threshold, curved two-harmonic frontier, and universal (not merely finite-site strictly positive) critical boundary provide substantively different predictions from Poisson analogues. Exact quadratic parameter tests and an explicit negative-energy witness make the claim useful for covariance model admissibility, rather than being a simple normalization trick.
